newsitem.title: DENMARK: Phoenix shareholder sees no quick sale.
newsitem.headline: Phoenix shareholder sees no quick sale.

text.p: Denmark's LD pension fund, holder of a three percent stake in Phoenix Contractors, said on Tuesday that it saw no quick end to a takeover battle for the firm, where staff favour Norwegian bidder Rieber and Son but institutional investors prefer to sell to Denmark's Superfos .

"We do not think that it will be settled before the (March 7) expiry date for further bids. A lot of new offers can still come in," LD (Loenmodtagernes Dyrtidsfond) managing director Flemming Skov Jensen told Reuters.
LD controls eight percent of votes in Phoenix.

Rieber and Superfos last week both raised their bids, to 820 million crowns and 808 million respectively. A third suitor, Danish building contractor Marius Pedersen, announced that it would not increase its offer of 776 million crowns.
Like pension fund ATP, which has a 10.4 percent Phoenix stake, LD backs a sale to Superfos.
"We clearly support Superfos' bid if there is not much difference between the two top offers," Jensen said.
On Monday, Phoenix workers urged LD to support Rieber's offer, as the Norwegian firm promised to respect the Danish roadbuilder's autonomy and sack as few staff as possible.
After shareholders and directors met last Friday, Phoenix did not name a favoured suitor, saying it would first talk to Rieber and Superfos.
The scrabble for Phoenix is the first open takeover bidding in Denmark, where acquisitions have traditionally been announced only after they have been agreed in the boardroom.
At 1130 GMT the most-traded Phoenix C-share stood at 670 crowns on the Copenhagen Stock Exchange, compared to Rieber's offer of 655 crowns. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
